questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that it was an english speakning destination because it made it a lot eaiser for me to get local friends and to get to know the culture. It was also important that there was a lot of focus on the social aspect of the college life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a person at Trinity who were avalible for the Erasmus law-students at anytime. She was therefore a really big help because it could be difficult to find the information online.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was introduction meetings and oppertunities to ask qustions. However everything was very confusing in the beginning and I could have used a bit more guidance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was really lucky and I did not have too much problems with housing, but Dublin is in general a really difficult city to find housing in. The prices are crazy and a lot of my Erasmus friends ended up staying at hostels through their entire stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is really difficult to find housing. Go into the housing market with an open mind and start early with the search.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Most of it was through email and the contact person was really nice and answered quick.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A contact person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful the only problem was that one of the classes that I wanted was removed to the spring semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: start early so it will not be too stressful and write to the contact person if you have questions. They are really helpfull.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I really like my courses but I would say that some of it was a bit eaiser than at KU. However it is ofcoruse a bit for difficult to study in another language and some of the exams was in hand, without any books or dictionary. In general it was very much up to yourself how much time you wanted to spend on the ready etc. but it was of coruse eaiser to pas the exam if you read more than the minimum.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a bit more up to the student to choose what to read. Personally I liked it, but I guess it depends on what you prefer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Medical law and ethics
International Public Law 
European Human Rights Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
European Human Rights Law. 

There was a really good teacher whit a lot of personal experience at the coruse, and the style of teaching was really great. I Learned a lot of new things eventhough I have had a smillar subject at KU.

questions.answer: I used a lot of money on traveling around the country.

questions.answer: I was really luckey with housing but you should expect to use around 7000-8000 DKK pr. month on housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is 120 different societies at Trinity so you can do basic everything from sport to star-watching

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sport team and the sport center at Trinity. The sport center is cheap and you can do a lot of great things. Also join some of the other societies, it is a really good way to get to know the local students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Everything. Ireland have so much great nature so it is perfect to go away for hicking in the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was Pretty easy because you could understand the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies and get ready for a great pub culture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything really challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open Irish people is to other cultures and meeting new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join societies. 
Ask your teachers if you have questions. 
Be openminded.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: To start the registration process early.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life at Trinity.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
